bios.name: Hannah Amundsen
bios.metaDescription: Hannah E. Amundsen is an associate at Blanchet LLP focused on commercial litigation, product liability, mass tort, toxic tort, and life sciences disputes.

Before beginning her law practice, Hannah worked in government and politics, experience that informs how she approaches matters shaped by public institutions, regulatory context, and competing constituencies.

Hannah brings a thoughtful, organized approach to complex records and evolving disputes. She focuses on understanding the facts early, keeping the work moving, and helping the team prepare each matter with the client's objective in view.

bios.name: Joel Blanchet
bios.metaDescription: Joel Blanchet is a trial lawyer representing sophisticated clients in commercial, environmental, product liability, and other high-stakes disputes.
introduction: Joel Blanchet is a trial lawyer and problem solver who represents companies, legal departments, executives, and other sophisticated clients in high-stakes disputes across the country. His work spans commercial litigation, environmental and toxic-tort matters, product liability, securities, intellectual property, bankruptcy, and government-facing disputes.

Before launching Blanchet LLP, Joel spent more than a decade as a partner in the litigation department at Kirkland & Ellis and later helped lead the litigation practice at Phillips Lytle. He has handled trials, arbitrations, appeals, and complex pretrial proceedings across industries and jurisdictions.

Joel stays close to the work and to the client. He brings practical business judgment to serious disputes, develops the record with trial in mind, and focuses the strategy on the result the client actually needs.
representativeExperience: Obtaining a complete defense judgment for Dow at the trial-court level after a 2025 bench trial in MDR Hotels, defeating negligence, nuisance, and trespass claims seeking more than $40 million.

Representing Dow in major CERCLA and 1,4-dioxane matters, including federal Superfund cost-recovery litigation, coordinated New York public water-provider actions, and New Jersey's statewide natural-resource damages action.
Securing summary judgment for Dow on more than $100 million in claims arising from a Louisiana natural gas leak while also obtaining substantial recoveries on counterclaims.
Securing summary judgment or dismissal of claims brought by more than 200 plaintiffs in June v. Union Carbide, with the judgments affirmed by the Tenth Circuit.

Serving as primary counsel to Columbus McKinnon and Magnetek in product-liability matters involving industrial hoists, chains, and material-handling equipment across the country, including dismissals and insurance recoveries.

Representing Dow in its long-running dispute with NOVA Chemicals over a jointly owned ethane cracker in Alberta, including trial responsibility for the plant-capacity issue central to the damages case.
Representing Dow in litigation over its approximately $15 billion agreement to acquire Rohm and Haas, resolved on the first day of trial with a reduction in the cash consideration paid.
Defending Osram Sylvania in Nilssen, where fifteen patents were held unenforceable and the client was awarded more than $6.1 million in fees and costs.
Defending Briggs & Stratton in nationwide multidistrict consumer-fraud litigation involving more than fifty proposed classes, resolved favorably before discovery.
Representing Fortune 100 companies in confidential SEC, internal, and regulatory investigations.

bios.name: Timothy Cronin
bios.metaDescription: Timothy Cronin is a litigator advising clients in complex commercial, product liability, toxic tort, and environmental disputes.
introduction: Timothy Cronin is a litigator who advises clients in complex commercial, product liability, toxic tort, and environmental disputes. His practice focuses on helping companies navigate high-stakes litigation and regulatory challenges involving technical, scientific, and environmental issues.

Tim has represented a Fortune 500 chemical company in matters involving allegations of groundwater contamination brought by state and regulatory agencies across multiple jurisdictions. He works closely with clients and litigation teams on matters requiring extensive factual development, management of large technical records, coordination of expert evidence, and strategic case execution.

Tim assists clients through all phases of litigation, including discovery, motion practice, and trial support. He approaches each matter with a focus on efficiency, thoughtful risk assessment, and achieving favorable outcomes for clients in complex disputes.

In addition to his commercial and environmental litigation practice, Tim maintains an active commitment to pro bono service, representing individuals in civil rights matters including claims involving Eighth Amendment violations. Before entering full-time litigation practice, he gained experience in personal injury and mergers and acquisitions matters.

Tim earned his J.D. from DePaul University College of Law, where he was a member of the National Trial Team, and earned his B.A. from DePaul University. He is admitted to practice in Illinois and is an Honoree of the New York State Bar Association's Empire State Counsel Program for Pro Bono Work.
Tim is a member of the Illinois State Bar Association and the American Bar Association's Toxic Torts and Environmental Law Committee.

bios.name: Andrew Devine
bios.metaDescription: Andrew Devine is a partner at Blanchet LLP who handles product liability, environmental, class and mass action, commercial, construction, investment, and CERCLA-related disputes.
introduction: Andy is a litigator who handles hard-to-resolve disputes with a strategic, practical, and tech-savvy approach.

Andy represents multinational corporations, manufacturers, construction owners and general contractors, banks, and investment companies in product liability, environmental, class and mass action, personal injury, commercial, construction, and investment matters in federal and state courts and arbitrations across the country.

He starts with the result a client is after, shapes an efficient and focused path to get there, and executes. Clients rely on him to manage complexity, including high-volume discovery, depositions, and expert practice, motion and appellate briefing, and removal and jurisdictional issues.

Andy brings particular depth to environmental disputes, including the defense of claims involving groundwater and the remediation of sites under CERCLA. He is also comfortable with the technology that defines modern litigation, using experience and e-discovery tools to surface the facts that matter.

He is especially valuable where litigation risk, government scrutiny, and appellate issues overlap, and where trial counsel is needed to assist or replace litigation counsel.
